 Advertisement Updated: 5:00 AM PDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ariel Roblin President & General Manager Opinion Ariel Roblin: Get informed and then vote for the Nov. 3 election
 Updated: 5:00 AM PDT Oct 25, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ariel Roblin President & General Manager Election Day is around the corner and if you have not started your research on the issues yet, now is a great time. 
 The constant push of campaign ads and social media posts never tell the whole story. In fact, they tell very little and are extremely biased - by design. 
 Advertisement So doing your own homework is important. This is a big election. Our congressional map has changed; we are choosing the next governor of California, as well as every elected state office, and there are several propositions on the table. 
 In the last midterm election, only 42.9% of registered voters in California voted. So less than half of registered voters decided on the future of California. 
 Maybe that's because people didn't feel informed or it felt overwhelming. 
 Hi, we're KCRA and we're here to help. At KCRA, we've been working to deliver you the facts and information you need all year long. 
 Across 68 hours of local news each week, we help you to understand how these issues and candidates may impact you. 
 You can find our Voter Guide on the KCRA app offering information about the candidates and propositions, with links to learn more. 
 You can also download the Very Local app and watch past episodes of California Politics 360, for an even closer look at the issues, helping you to be informed when you vote. 
 Whether you decide to vote early or in person on Nov. 3, turn to sources you can trust and make your voice heard. 
 Your vote helps shape our future. 
 Make it an informed one and help your neighbor as well. Let's try to get over 50% this time.
 Ariel Roblin is the president and general manager of KCRA 3 and My58. See more of her editorials here .
